record.paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
record.original_question: Is every spherical set Ramsey, meaning that for every number of colors r there is a dimension threshold N such that every r-coloring of Euclidean N-space contains a monochromatic congruent copy of the set?

evidence.quote: It is shown in [8] that any Ramsey set must lie on the surface of a sphere (in some dimension) – we call such sets spherical. In particular, collinear sets, as pointed out above, can always be avoided with at most 16 colors in any number of dimensions. It may turn out that the Ramsey sets are very easy to describe: Conjecture 3. ($1000). Every spherical set is Ramsey.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a finite set $X \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ Ramsey if for every positive integer $r$ there exists a positive integer $N = N(X,r)$ such that for every $r$-coloring of $\mathbb{R}^N$ there exists a monochromatic subset of $\mathbb{R}^N$ that is congruent (i.e., isometric via a Euclidean isometry) to $X$. Call a finite set $X \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ spherical if it lies on the surface of some Euclidean sphere (equivalently, $X$ is contained in some sphere $S^{k-1}(c,\rho) \subset \mathbb{R}^k$ of finite radius).

Prove or disprove: every finite spherical set is Ramsey.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (Graham's $1000 conjecture) that every spherical set is Ramsey remains open as of 2026. It is one of the central problems of Euclidean Ramsey theory; a rival conjecture by Leader–Russell–Walters (that the Ramsey sets are precisely subsets of transitive sets) and recent work (e.g., counterexamples to related diameter-Ramsey conjectures, and partial results via higher-order Fourier analysis) leave the status unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Transitive Sets in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Graham conjectured that a set is Ramsey if and only if it is spherical... we propose a rival conjecture that the Ramsey sets are precisely the transitive sets.
status_evidence.claim: The spherical-Ramsey conjecture is still the central conjecture and remains open, prompting alternative conjectures.

status_evidence.title: THE BIGGEST OPEN PROBLEM IN EUCLIDEAN RAMSEY THEORY
status_evidence.snippet: The outstanding open problem in Euclidean Ramsey theory is to determine the Ramsey sets.
status_evidence.claim: The characterization of Ramsey sets, including Graham's spherical conjecture, remains an outstanding open problem.

status_evidence.title: Non-spherical sets versus lines in Euclidean Ramsey theory
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on spherical vs non-spherical sets in Euclidean Ramsey theory.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2024) work treats the spherical Ramsey question as still open.
